newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST--Italy Q3 GDP seen rising 0.4 percent. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Italy Q3 GDP seen rising 0.4 percent. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Italy's third quarter 1996 gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to have grown on average by 0.44 percent over the second quarter and by some 0.48 percent compared to the third quarter of 1995, economists said.
Italy's official statistics body ISTAT is set to release preliminary GDP data on Friday November 29 at 0800 GMT.
In the second quarter of 1996, GDP rose 0.4 percent on the previous quarter and 0.7 percent on a year-on-year basis.
The forecasts are based on weekly studies by five brokers with the range of forecasts expecting a 0.3-0.7 percent rise over the previous quarter, and a 0.1-0.8 percent increase over year ago levels.

Most of the five studies see a GDP rise for the whole of 1996 of 0.8 percent, except for Credito Italiano which sees a rise of 1.0 percent. At the end of September, the Italian government revised its own forecast to a rise of 0.8 percent from a previous rise of 1.2 percent.
According to Comit, the rise in the third quarter GDP will be due to a small rise in consumption after a stagnation in previous periods and positive trade figures (Corrects data.)
San Paolo said the positive trend in private consumption in the quarter, up 0.5 percent, would compensate for the negative trend in public consumption.
